advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a check on the result to `test_fast_import_stream_is_sent_as_lf_bytes`: read back the imported blob with `git cat-file -p <sha>:a.txt` and assert it equals "x\ny\n" exactly. Keep or loosen the kwargs check so it is not the only assertion.
evidence:
tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py:264-268: `def capture(cmd, *args, **kwargs):
        if cmd[:2] == ["git", "fast-import"]:
            sent.append(kwargs.get("input"))
            assert not kwargs.get("text") and "encoding" not in kwargs`

tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py:276-278: `(payload,) = sent
    assert isinstance(payload, bytes)
    assert b"\r" not in payload`
tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py:274: the return value of `_fast_import_history(...)` (the shas) is thrown away, and the imported content is never read back.
advisory.finding: The new test `test_fast_import_stream_is_sent_as_lf_bytes` breaks if the helper is refactored without any change in behavior. It checks the exact `subprocess.run` keyword arguments (`text`, `encoding`, `input`) of the fast-import call. If the helper switched to `subprocess.Popen(...).communicate(bytes)`, or wrote the stream to a binary temp file and passed it as `stdin=`, it would still deliver the same LF-only stream to fast-import. The test would still fail: `sent` would be empty, so `(payload,) = sent` raises ValueError, or `input` would be None. It never checks what fast-import actually produced, such as the imported blob content or the returned sha.
scenarios: A maintainer changes the helper to use `Popen.communicate` or to feed fast-import from a binary file via `stdin=`. The helper still works on every OS, but this test fails with a ValueError because nothing was recorded in `sent`.
advisory.suggested_fix: Keep the returned shas: `(sha,) = _fast_import_history(...)`. Then assert `subprocess.run(["git", "cat-file", "-p", f"{sha}:a.txt"], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True).stdout == b"x\ny\n"`. This checks the imported bytes alongside the bytes-input check, so the test stays useful if the helper's subprocess call changes.
